newsitem.title: USA: Commerce committee may want hearing on US bank law.
newsitem.headline: Commerce committee may want hearing on US bank law.

text.p: Legislators on the House Banking Committee said Monday the House Commerce Committee may want to hold hearings on financial sector reform.
Although the Banking Committee has primary jurisdiction over banking reform measures, that jurisdiction is not exclusive, Banking Committee chairman Jim Leach said.

The question of other committees holding hearings, which could delay consideration of a bill by the full House, has "yet to be resolved," Leach, Republican of Iowa, said at a meeting of the Institute of International bankers here.
The issue remains "pretty uncertain," Rep. John LaFalce, a leading Banking Committee Democrat, added: "I would be amazed if the Commerce Committee didn't want to get its mitts on this somehow."

In the Senate, Leach said he saw a possibility of accelerated action by the Senate Banking Committee. While the issue remains under review in the Senate, there are "some reasons to believe" the Senate might act quickly on bank reform, Leach said.
LaFalce said the chance for reform passing might depend on the the Clinton administration's level of involvement.

Suggesting that Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin and even the President himself should get involved in pushing bank reform, LaFalce said a high-level push "might be necessary to produce the type of product the adminstration wants."
